name: Emberá-Tadó
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog embe1261 lists only wordlists (Valencia et al. 1991 vocabulario ilustrado tadó; Huber & Reed 1992) and ethnography; no grammar/phonology of the Tadó variety located.

new_statements.quote: Estos son los únicos signos modales. Para la acentuación pinto el acento allí donde lo he oído de viva voz, pues por regla general puede asentarse que el acento carga sobre la última sílaba.
new_statements.translation: These are the only modal signs. For accentuation I write the accent where I have heard it from the living voice, since as a general rule it can be stated that the stress falls on the last syllable.
new_statements.citation: Uribe, José Vicente (author), copied and edited by J. M. Quijano Otero. 1882. Gramática y vocabulario de la lengua que hablan los indios que habitan la región comprendida entre las desembocaduras del Atrato, en el Atlántico, y del San Juan, en el Pacífico, y la cordillera en que limitan las antiguas provincias del Chocó y Antioquia. In: Congreso Internacional de Americanistas, Actas de la cuarta reunión, Madrid 1881, tomo 2, pp. 297-309. Madrid: Fortanet.
new_statements.locator: p. 299, 'Indicaciones generales', subsection 'Signos' (PDF page 311 of the archive.org volume scan)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: read directly; the page (section 'INDICACIONES GENERALES / SIGNOS', third paragraph) reads exactly: 'Estos son los únicos signos modales. Para la acentuación pinto el acento allí donde lo he oído de viva voz, pues por regla general puede asentarse que el acento carga sobre la última sílaba.' (the print has a typographic space before the comma after 'voz'; the companion misreads 'acento' as 'acepto' and 'sobre' as 'sobi*e', but the image is correct). Locator checked against the whole-volume scan../nort2972/526 pp., no text layer): PDF p. 309 is the title page 'Gramática y vocabulario de la lengua que hablan los indios DARIENES, que habitan la región comprendida entre las d…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable as a general rule; the author writes an accent mark only where he heard it, i.e. on the words that depart from that rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Implied: words carry a written accent where the author heard stress elsewhere than the final syllable; no list or rule for the exceptions is given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (citation forms in a 19th-century amateur grammar/vocabulary); no discussion of phrase-level accent. The description is an aggregate of the Emberá spoken between the Atrato and San Juan mouths and the Chocó-Antioquia cordillera, not a Tadó-specific one. Modern first-hand data for Tadó (Huber & Reed 1992 wordlist, 315/396 forms stress-marked; Harms 1989 comparative list) carry accent marks but no rule; the closest modern relative, Emberá-Chamí (Aguirre Licht), is described as default-penultimate with weight-sensitive and morphologically driven shifts, and Constenla & Margery 1991 report final-or-penult in Catío/Sambú, so the 1882 'final' rule should be treated as provisional for Tadó.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is from Uribe 1882 (Spanish edition of the 1876 ZfE 'Bericht'), a 19th-century aggregate description of the Emberá language of the region between the Atrato and San Juan mouths and the Chocó-Antioquia cordillera; the 1876 title enumerates the Chamíes, Andáguedas, Murindoes, Cañasgordas, Rioverdes, Necodaes, Caramantas, Tadocitos, Patoes and Curasambas as its speakers, so it covers Tadó (embe1261) together with Emberá-Chamí (embe1262) and the Antioquia Catío groups (embe1260 / nort2972); the sibling nort2972 audit uses the same source. No Tadó-specific phonology or grammar could be opened; the Tadó-specific works (Pickens 1999a-c, Valencia et al. 1991) are SIL manuscripts/publications not reachable from our machine.

sources.locator: p. 299, 'Indicaciones generales', subsection 'Signos' (PDF page 311 of the archive.org volume scan)
sources.note: p. 299 'Indicaciones generales / Signos': the author writes the accent where he heard it, 'pues por regla general puede asentarse que el acento carga sobre la última sílaba' (general rule: stress on the last syllable). Aggregate 19th-c. description of the Emberá of the Chocó-Antioquia region, whose 1876 German version names the Tadocitos among the groups covered; not a Tadó-specific description.

sources.citation: Constenla Umaña, Adolfo & Enrique Margery Peña. 1991. Elementos de fonología comparada chocó. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 17(1-2): 137-191.
sources.note: sec. 2.3 'Acento' pp. 151-152: stress 'recae en la penúltima sílaba casi sin excepciones en saija y chami... en tanto que en catio y sambú puede recaer lo mismo en la penúltima que en la última'; reconstructs free accent for proto-Emberá. Tadó is NOT among the varieties compared.

sources.citation: Harms, Phillip Lee. 1984. Fonología del epena pedee (saija). Sistemas fonológicos de idiomas colombianos 5. Bogotá: ILV.
sources.note: Mentions Tadó only in the list of Chocó languages (p. 2 of intro); stress statements concern Epena Saija, not Tadó.

sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PM5191.H82 1992 (also: hathitrust digitized, search-only (in copyright))
sources.note: 396 'embera Tadó' forms, 315 with an acute stress mark (kʰĩrãmé 'tongue', itʰái 'mouth', kʰíɗa 'tooth', boɾó 'head', osotʰáu 'neck', makʰaɾá 'thigh'); mostly final-marked in the sample but no rule stated in the data file. The book's introductory notes (which may explain the stress marking) were not obtainable: MPG PuRe PDF audience-restricted (401), HathiTrust search-only.

sources.citation: Harms, Phillip L. (comp.). 1989 [pages dated Julio 1990]. Comparative Word List of Chocoan Languages. Prepublication draft. SIL (SIL Language and Culture Archives).
sources.note: Has a TD = 'Ebéra Tado' column (Playa de Oro, Chocó; collected by Phillip Harms) with acute accent marks on forms (e.g. kiramé 'tongue'), but the introduction gives no stress rule; data only.

sources.citation: Loewen, Jacob A. 1960. Dialectología de la familia lingüística chocó. Revista Colombiana de Antropología 9: 9-22.
sources.note: Lists Tadó as one of nine Epera dialects (~1000 speakers, isogloss table); segmental isoglosses only, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Anon. [J. V. Uribe, tr. 'B.']. 1876. Bericht über die Sprache, welche die Chamies-, Angáguedas-, Murindoes-, Cañasgordas-, Rioverdes-, Necodaes-, Caramantas-, Tadocitos-, Patoes- und Curasambas-Indianer sprechen. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 8: 359-378.
sources.note: p. 359 'Allgemeine Bemerkungen / Zeichen': 'Für die Accentuation ist der Accent dahin gesetzt, wo ich das Wort habe betonen hören' — accent written where heard; the 'last syllable as a general rule' clause of the 1882 Spanish version is absent here. Title explicitly lists the Tadocitos as speakers of the language described.
